=== PUBLIC TURN 1/2 ===
The `converge` round role proposal is complete. The supplied proposals remain unresolved until authority-based adjudication; no vote or perspective execution has occurred.

Suggested seats: Privacy & Compliance: 1; Delivery Engineering: 1; Mobile Product: 1; FinOps: 1.

- Privacy & Compliance — `privacy-regulatory`
  - Lens: Which options comply with the prohibition on exposing patient names or appointment reasons to third-party push providers?
  - Invited for: Binding regulatory constraints.
  - Owns: Third-party payload privacy and authenticated-content boundaries.
  - Excludes: Latency optimization, reliability design, and cost selection.
  - Evidence: Supplied regulatory and opaque-identifier authorities.
  - Deliverable: Compliance determination for every proposal.
  - Authority limit: Cannot prohibit compliant channels without evidence.
  - Constraints: Read-only; `converge`; no voting.
  - Role revision: `privacy-regulatory-r1`
  - Provenance: Main-generated; no parent revision.

- Delivery Engineering — `delivery-reliability`
  - Lens: Which compliant approach meets the 30-second requirement through failures?
  - Invited for: Delivery latency, fallback behavior, and existing-platform compatibility.
  - Owns: Push/WebSocket usage, failure recovery, foreground fallback, and timeliness.
  - Excludes: Interpreting regulation or making cost override mandatory.
  - Evidence: Supplied platform capabilities and 30-second requirement.
  - Deliverable: Reliability assessment and minimum viable delivery flow.
  - Authority limit: May optimize only within privacy and authentication constraints.
  - Constraints: Read-only; `converge`; no new unbounded architecture.
  - Role revision: `delivery-reliability-r1`
  - Provenance: Main-generated; no parent revision.

- Mobile Product — `mobile-client-experience`
  - Lens: Can the app surface status within 30 seconds while fetching protected details only after authentication?
  - Invited for: Client-visible behavior and authenticated retrieval feasibility.
  - Owns: Opaque-event handling, authenticated detail fetch, foreground behavior, and status semantics.
  - Excludes: Relaxing privacy rules or choosing solely by vendor price.
  - Evidence: Supplied Mobile App capability and user-facing timing requirement.
  - Deliverable: Client-flow assessment for every proposal.
  - Authority limit: User experience cannot override regulation.
  - Constraints: Read-only; `converge`; no voting.
  - Role revision: `mobile-client-experience-r1`
  - Provenance: Main-generated; no parent revision.

- FinOps — `delivery-cost`
  - Lens: Among approaches satisfying all mandatory constraints, which minimizes incremental and operating cost?
  - Invited for: Cost is relevant only after feasibility and compliance.
  - Owns: Relative vendor-message, polling-load, and reuse costs.
  - Excludes: Treating lowest cost as sufficient when an option violates authority.
  - Evidence: Supplied existing-provider/gateway baseline; explicitly identify unavailable cost data.
  - Deliverable: Constraint-qualified cost comparison.
  - Authority limit: Cost is a tie-breaker, not a hard-constraint override.
  - Constraints: Read-only; `converge`; no unsupported price assumptions.
  - Role revision: `delivery-cost-r1`
  - Provenance: Main-generated; no parent revision.

Planned risk coverage:

- Regulatory payload restriction: Privacy & Compliance — critical
- 30-second status requirement: Delivery Engineering and Mobile Product — critical
- Authenticated protected-content retrieval: Privacy & Compliance and Mobile Product — critical
- Delivery failure and fallback: Delivery Engineering — critical
- Existing push/WebSocket compatibility: Delivery Engineering and FinOps
- Operating cost: FinOps

Overlap is intentional for cross-checking critical boundaries; no critical surface is uncovered. No blocking conflicts or acknowledgement warnings are active.

Plan revision: `notification-converge-plan-r1`  
Plan digest: unavailable in this chat-only, non-persisted evaluation; the complete displayed slate is the freeze reference.

To run the adjudication, reply: `Accept the exact displayed notification-converge-plan-r1 slate and start.` You may instead edit, add, remove, merge, split, or reset roles.

=== PUBLIC TURN 2/2 ===
Decision: adopt Proposal 3—send only an opaque event ID through push, display a non-sensitive status, fetch protected details after authentication, and use foreground polling as fallback.

This is an architecture decision, not rollout approval. Before release, end-to-end tests must prove status appears within 30 seconds during normal delivery and fallback. Polling must leave processing margin below the 30-second limit.

Proposal dispositions:

- Proposal 1, full-body push: `rejected`. It can expose expressly prohibited patient information.
- Proposal 2, ban push and poll every 30 seconds: `rejected`. Regulation restricts push content, not the channel. A 30-second polling interval also leaves no demonstrated margin for processing and display.
- Proposal 3, opaque push plus authenticated fetch and fallback: `accepted`, subject to the mandatory timing gate above.
- Proposal 4, select solely by vendor cost: `rejected`. Cost cannot override privacy or timing requirements. It remains a secondary optimization criterion after compliance; no supplied data establishes a cost winner.

The material conflict was resolved by authority, not votes. Privacy initially found polling permissible, while reliability questioned Proposal 3’s timing evidence. Deliberation established that Proposal 2 is privacy-compatible but unjustifiably overbroad, and that Proposal 3 can be selected architecturally while its timing evidence remains a rollout gate.

Public evidence ledger:

| ID | Disposition | Finding | Sources | Supplied evidence locator |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| E1 | Rejected | Full-body push violates the content prohibition | `privacy-regulatory-r1`, `delivery-reliability-r1`, `mobile-client-experience-r1`, `delivery-cost-r1` | Regulatory prohibition; Proposal 1 |
| E2 | Rejected | A blanket push ban lacks authority and 30-second polling lacks timing margin | `privacy-regulatory-r1`, `delivery-reliability-r1`, `mobile-client-experience-r1` | Opaque-ID permission; 30-second requirement; Proposal 2 |
| E3 | Accepted | Opaque push plus authenticated retrieval matches the authorized boundary | All four role revisions | Mobile capability; existing push/WebSocket services; Proposal 3 |
| E4 | Required gate | Normal and fallback paths must demonstrate status display within 30 seconds | `delivery-reliability-r1`, `mobile-client-experience-r1` | 30-second requirement; Proposal 3 fallback |
| E5 | Rejected | Lowest cost alone is not a valid selection rule | `delivery-cost-r1`, `privacy-regulatory-r1`, `delivery-reliability-r1`, `mobile-client-experience-r1` | Mandatory constraints; Proposal 4 |
| E6 | Residual risk | Relative push and polling costs cannot be determined | `delivery-cost-r1` | No pricing, volume, or polling-load data supplied |

Gate: `continue` with Proposal 3; rollout remains blocked until E4 passes.
